rows.evidence: Q1: Data and Method <U+2013> 11 monitoring wells read twice monthly 2008<U+2013>2010 plus 336 soil samples in four farmlands and shelterbelts in Kalamiji Oasis. Q2: Abstract and Results (Figure 2) <U+2013> groundwater level declined on average about 0.5 m per year over the two-year observation period, which the authors relate to the large-scale implementation of drip irrigation from 2008 to 2010, with conserved water used on newly reclaimed land. Q6: Results/Conclusions <U+2013> the decline is reported for the Kalamiji Oasis as a whole, from wells distributed across the oasis (district scale, not a single plot). Q8: Discussion <U+2013> the authors state the groundwater decline is only 'suspected' to result from drip irrigation and that further monitoring is needed to confirm it; the observation period is only about two years; they also note farmers' pumping during the irrigation season as an alternative driver of the seasonal drawdown.
rows.notes: Support for the claim is weak and indirect: there is no flood-versus-drip comparison, the attribution of the decline to drip adoption is hedged ('may be related', 'suspected'), and the authors also attribute the seasonal drawdown to farmers pumping groundwater and to expansion of irrigated area with saved water. Only well monitoring is used (no second method for recharge); return flow or deep percolation is not measured. Q5: four wells on loamy, sandy and clay soils within one oasis, but the decline is reported as an oasis average, not evaluated per soil, and a single region/climate. Q7: no condition is stated from own findings as a requirement for the effect. Q9: decline given as an average (0.5 m/yr in abstract and results; 0.25 m/yr in conclusions) with a seasonal range of 1.0<U+2013>1.3 m but no dispersion for the annual decline rate.

notes: Full text appears complete. Internal inconsistency in the reported groundwater decline rate (0.5 m/yr in abstract and results; 0.25 m/yr in r<U+00E9>sum<U+00E9> and conclusions). The paper is primarily about soil salinity in shelterbelts versus farmland; the groundwater<U+2013>drip link is a secondary, cautiously stated observation.
